newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A high-powered committee, established to assist Constitutional Affairs Minister Valli Moosa, met for the first time last week to develop a policy which will see local government in SA dramatically changed before the 1999 elections.
- Multinational companies that win lucrative SA state and parastatal business will be required to set up businesses locally, a move expected to accelerate the pace of foreign investments.

- Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils has defended government's decision to rehire sacked chemical warfare expert and alleged drug dealer Wouter Basson, saying the consequences of allowing him to "go freelance" would have been "too ghastly to contemplate".
- The Western Cape needed to be compensated for the huge influx of people from the Eastern Cape, local government official Peter Marais said at the weekend.

- The Small Business Development Corporation (SBDC) has been accused of racial bias in its lending operations last week by a group of parliamentarians who visited eight of the nine provinces in November to evaluate progress with government's new small business promotion strategy.

- Saflife, the listed company being used as the vehicle for the acquisition by African Mining Group (AMG) of a 34,9 percent stake in JCI Ltd, will be transformed into a mining and financial services group with a net asset value of about four billion rands after its proposed 2.4 billion rand share issue, said Mzi Khumalo, who is part of the shareholder pool that controls Saflife.

- A strong performance by its new titles ans stringent cash-flow management supported Independent Newspaper's solid 25 percent increase in earnings a share to 167.8 cents in the year to December 31 from 134.6 cents in the previous year, John Featherstone, the chief executive, said last week.

- The Communications Workers' Union walked out of wage talks with Telkom on Friday and threatened to strike in a bid to discourage a multibillion-rand investment by a foreign strategic equity partner.

- The top-level probe into South African rugby looks set to get more muscle this week with the likely inclusion of tax expert Michael Katz and former High Court judge and businessman Mervyn King in the task force to probe alleged irregularities in the sport.

- The decision to re-employ sacked chemical warfare expert and alleged drug dealer Wouter Basson was not a secret and was done in the best interests of the country, Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said last night.
- The death of South Africa's most experienced glider pilot on the West Rand on Saturday was one on the most horrific accidents yet witnessed by local officials, ambulance staff said on Sunday.
- A man was savaged to death on Saturday by two pit bull terriers which were allegedly provoked by a third party into attacking him and a woman in Melville.
